subject: storytime
title: Cinderella
about: Charles Perrault's Cinderella, kept short and kind: a girl who does all the work for her unkind stepsisters, a fairy godmother who makes a dress and a golden coach from a pumpkin, a dance that must end by midnight, and a glass slipper that fits only her. First graders love the pumpkin coach and the clock striking twelve, and the ending shows Cinderella forgiving her stepsisters, with the lesson said plainly: be kind, even when others are not. It is a public-domain story retold here in first-grade words, five pages long.
tip: Count the bongs of the clock together, then ask why Cinderella hugged her stepsisters at the end.

book.author: Charles Perrault (retold)
book.source: public domain, retold in first-grade words
book.blurb: A pumpkin coach, a midnight dash, and one glass slipper.

passage.text:
Once there was a kind girl named Cinderella.
She lived with her stepmother and two stepsisters.
The stepsisters were not kind.
They made her do all the work.
She swept the floors.
She washed the pots.
She slept by the fire.
But she was always kind to them.
***
One day, the prince had a grand ball.
Everyone wanted to go and dance.
The stepsisters put on their best dresses.
"You cannot come," they said.
"You have nothing to wear."
Off they went.
Cinderella sat by the fire and cried.
***
Just then, a fairy godmother appeared.
"You shall go to the ball," she said.
She waved her wand.
A pumpkin turned into a golden coach.
Four mice turned into four white horses.
Cinderella's rags turned into a lovely dress.
On her feet were two glass slippers.
"Be home by midnight," said the fairy godmother.
"At midnight, the magic ends."
***
At the ball, the prince saw Cinderella.
"Will you dance with me?" he asked.
They danced and danced.
Then the clock began to strike twelve.
Bong! Bong! Bong!
"I must go!" said Cinderella.
She ran down the steps.
One glass slipper fell off her foot.
She did not stop to get it.
The prince picked it up.
***
The next day, the prince went from house to house.
"Who fits this slipper?" he asked.
The stepsisters tried it on.
It did not fit.
Then Cinderella tried it on.
It fit just right!
"We are sorry we were unkind," said the stepsisters.
"I forgive you," said Cinderella, and she hugged them.
Cinderella and the prince were married.
Be kind, even when others are not.

cards.q: Who made Cinderella do all the work?
cards.note: The stepsisters were not kind: she swept, washed and slept by the fire, and stayed kind anyway.

cards.q: What did the fairy godmother turn into a coach?
cards.note: One wave of the wand: a pumpkin became a golden coach and four mice became four white horses.

cards.q: What did Cinderella lose on the steps?
cards.note: It fell off her foot as she ran, and the prince picked it up.
The fairy godmother said to be home by midnight, and the clock striking twelve is midnight.

cards.q: What happened first in the story?
cards.note: Sweeping, washing and sleeping by the fire come first; the fairy godmother comes after the ball starts.

cards.q: What happened at the end of the story?
cards.note: The slipper fit, the stepsisters said sorry, and Cinderella and the prince were married.

cards.q: How did Cinderella feel when she was left at home?
cards.note: The stepsisters went off to the ball and she sat by the fire and cried.
Be kind, even when others are not: Cinderella stayed kind and even forgave her stepsisters.

cards.q: In the story, what is a 'ball'?
cards.note: Not the round toy: in this story a ball is a grand party where everyone dances.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: He reads the three words himself; only one of them is in the story.
